blocks.body:
## Technical summary

The existing production runs still identify replica-ladder transport as the large-lattice problem, but the copied A6000 grid does not provide a valid equilibrium test of the proposed ladders. Those pilots used the conservative startup integrator for their entire duration, ended before the prescribed L^3 startup stage, never reset exchange diagnostics, and compared noisy block-end magnetizations. Their all-reject result must not be used to choose or discard a production profile. The corrected workflow now separates discarded startup from equilibrium measurement.

## HMC remains healthy while transport collapses

Median HMC acceptance stays between 73% and 78% from L=12 through L=32. In contrast, median minimum edge acceptance falls to 0.1% at L=32 and all 30 L=32 tasks record zero round trips. L=24 is intermediate: 14 of 30 tasks have zero round trips. This divergence identifies ladder overlap and diffusion as the primary lever.

## Existing L=24 Binder windows are not decision-safe

The three L=24 scans warn on 230, 256, and 248 of 301 targets at Z=-0.6, -0.77, and -0.9. Applying the stricter critical-window contract—ESS at least 50, ESS fraction at least 1%, top-1 M4 contribution at most 50%, and at least two usable source points—rejects every sampled row inside each crossing window. The validator emits new source points at both crossings, both ±0.01 edges, and the midpoint of the failing region.

## The copied pilot rejection is method-driven

L=24 pilots measured 8,192 sweeps although the prescribed cold-start stage is 13,824 sweeps; L=32 measured 16,384 versus a 32,768-sweep startup stage. Final minimum HMC acceptance remained 93%–96%, confirming that the conservative startup integrator never switched to the 70%–80% equilibrium regime. Low round-trip coverage and ordered/disordered separation are therefore expected cold-start outcomes. The edge-acceptance pattern is still useful for screening—especially the L=32 bottlenecks—but it is not sufficient for profile promotion or final rejection.

## Scope and metric definitions

The historical cohort is every completed task in the existing L=12, 16, 24, and 32 production manifests. A round trip is a labeled walker visit to the low-mass endpoint, then the high-mass endpoint, then the low endpoint again. The corrected rate denominator is exchange rounds, equal to HMC sweeps divided by `swap_every`. Walker coverage is the fraction of ladder walkers with at least one completed round trip. A critical window spans the two Binder levels U4=1/3 and U4=0.465 plus 0.01 in m2 on each side.

## Corrected method and promotion gates

Each corrected pilot runs the full L^3 cold-start schedule with the startup integrator, discards that state history, resets all HMC/swap/walker diagnostics, and then switches to the equilibrium HMC defaults for measured sweeps. Phase agreement uses block-mean target abs(M) from the final half of measurement blocks. Candidate promotion still requires every edge acceptance at least 20%, median edge acceptance at least 30%, no unused edge, at least half of walkers completing a round trip, and ordered/disordered agreement within two combined standard errors. Legacy CSVs lacking the block-mean phase metric are now rejected explicitly.

## Limitations and robustness checks

No corrected L=24/L=32 grid has completed yet, so no ladder is validated or scientifically rejected by the new protocol. The copied runs do show that L=32 uniform ladders with too few slots develop weak edges as span increases, which narrows the next candidate set. The original aggregate round-trip totals also used sweep denominators; corrected pilots reset diagnostics after startup and use exchange rounds. Orphan `.tmp.*` files are reported but were not deleted.

## Recommended next steps

1. Rerun a reduced corrected grid rather than repeating all 12 legacy candidates: L=24 with 17/0.3, 25/0.4, and 33/0.3; L=32 with 25/0.3, 33/0.3, and 33/0.4. Keep swaps every sweep.
2. Use a new run name so legacy files cannot be mixed with corrected outputs.
3. Promote only the smallest candidate that passes all gates at all three coordinates and both starts.
4. Only after promotion, run the critical-window source CSVs, reweight, and extract warning-free crossings.

## Further questions

Does a wider mass span actually connect the two basins at L=32, or is a second tempering coordinate required? How many exchange rounds are needed for stable walker-coverage estimates at each slot count? Once phase transport passes, does the existing equilibrium HMC trajectory length remain optimal at all three critical coordinates?
